title: Abraham (Abram)
summary: Son of Terah; called by God from Ur and Haran; father of the faithful (Gen 11–25).

sorting_basis.note: Tier 2: CFAH-1 Table 1 (Ussher-Jones baseline): 1996 BC (Birth of Abraham) (no higher-tier year available).

birth.citation: Griffith & White, "Chronological Framework of Ancient History. 1: Problem, Data, and Methodology," ARJ 15 (2022): 377–390, section "Our Assumptions (Declared Biases)", Table 1 "Biblically derived dates from Ussher and Jones"
birth.note: CFAH-1 Table 1 (Ussher-Jones biblical baseline adopted by CFAH); not a triangulated anchor point.

birth.citation: Jones, Chronology of the Old Testament (15th ed., 2002), p. 77 ("born BC 1996"); "Chronological Compendium", p. 1 (2008 AM)
Ussher, Annals of the World, Second Age §63 (paragraph numbering of the modern transcription)

birth.date: Birth of Abram: Anno Mundi 2008; 1922 B.C. (SBC)
birth.citation: Jordan, "Egypt in Biblical History," Biblical Chronology 5:8 (December 1993), chart "Anno Mundi / B.C. (SBC) / B.C. (CCC)" at the start of the article
birth.note: AM 2008 also in BC 2:6, 4:8 §2, 6:4 §8. B.C. year is Jordan's "SBC" (strictest Biblical chronology), which takes Daniel's 70 weeks literally from Cyrus (456 B.C. instead of the conventional 536 B.C.); not comparable one-to-one with Ussher/CFAH B.C. years.

birth.citation: Anno Mundi Chronology Studies (unnamed compiler; a compilation of James B. Jordan's system), p. 2, chart "Genesis 11:10 – 12 Genealogy"
birth.note: Agrees with Jordan's own published AM 2008.

birth.citation: Preparing the World for Jesus (1st ed., 2020), ch. 4 "First Empires in Mesopotamia (2360–1750 BC)", PDF p. 87 (printed p. 86)
birth.note: Born in Ur of the Chaldees; also p. 99 ("Born 2166 bc"). Timeline Review pairs it with an asterisked 1996 BC (the book's Ussher-chronology equivalent). (p. 114) Differs from the sort year (1996 BC, cfah-table1) by 170 years.
birth.edition_note: 1st ed. (2020); superseded by the 2nd ed. (2024), which prints "Abraham (1996 – 1819 BC)" (PDF p. 160): 170 years later.

birth.citation: Preparing the World for Jesus (2nd ed., 2024), ch. 7 "The Return of the Nephilim: Nimrod Attempts World Empire", PDF p. 160 (printed p. 146)
birth.note: Timeline Review 2; also p. 247. The text (p. 152) says Gilgamesh began ten years before Abram's birth.

birth.citation: Raleigh, The History of the World (1617, EEBO-TCP A10357), Chronological Table, sig. 782b
birth.note: Year cell "2691 2009 352". The third printed figure 352 is the column "Floud", not a length. To the Reader (sig. 780b): the Julian Period exceeds the yeere of the World by 682. The 175 at the end of the name is the lifespan he prints. The same section (Book II, ch. I, §VIII, sig. 164a) also prints "An. mundi 2008 dil. 352. natus Abraham, Eus. Aug. de Ciuit. Dei", introduced with "I conclude" and naming Eusebius and Augustine. The narrative sentence and the chronological table both print 2009. The 2008 is not given a second year. His table also prints the death at World 2183. 2009 + 175 is not 2183. Both figures are left as printed.

birth.date: which happened in the yeere of the World, 2009.
birth.citation: Raleigh, The History of the World (1617, EEBO-TCP A10357), Book II, ch. I, §VIII, sig. 164a
birth.note: Narrative sentence. The chronological table prints the same yeere of the World. To the Reader (sig. 780b): the Julian Period exceeds the yeere of the World by 682. No BC conversion.

birth.date: by the Hebrew chronology, that Abraham was born A. M. 2008
birth.citation: Shuckford, The Sacred and Profane History of the World Connected, 5th ed., revised by James Creighton (London: William Baynes, 1819), vol. 1, Book IV, p. 169 (facsimile PDF p. 265)
birth.note: He says this will appear hereafter very clearly. Page 251 prints A. M. 2001 for the same birth. Both are entered. See open question K3.

birth.date: Abram was born in the one hundred and thirtieth year of Terah, three hundred and fifty-two years after the Flood, A. M. 2001
birth.citation: Shuckford, The Sacred and Profane History of the World Connected, 5th ed., revised by James Creighton (London: William Baynes, 1819), vol. 1, Book V, p. 251 (facsimile PDF p. 347)
birth.note: Page 252 says he has fixed this birth by the Hebrew chronology. The same paragraph also says three hundred and fifty-two years after the Flood. Page 169 prints A. M. 2008. Not reconciled. The Tolle Lege facsimile prints a clear 1 in A. M. 2001. On Internet Archive leaf n344 the same sentence is present, and the last digit is blotted, so that leaf alone does not confirm 1 or 8. The year stored is the clear facsimile digit. See open question K3.

death.note: Not stated in the Jones sources read (Chart No. 1; Chronology of the Old Testament 15th ed. 2002, Chronological Compendium p. 1). Leave empty until verified.

death.citation: Ussher, Annals of the World, Third Age §101 (paragraph numbering of the modern transcription)

death.date: "Abraham died at the age of 175 (Gen. 25:7), in 2183"
death.citation: Jordan, "The Chronology of the Pentateuch (Part 3)," Biblical Chronology 6:5 (May 1994), §10 "The Chronological Structure of Abraham's Life"
Anno Mundi Chronology Studies (unnamed compiler; a compilation of James B. Jordan's system), p. 3, chart "Genesis 12 – 25 Chronology of Abraham’s Life"
death.note: Agrees with Jordan's own published AM 2183.

death.citation: Preparing the World for Jesus (2nd ed., 2024), ch. 7 "The Return of the Nephilim: Nimrod Attempts World Empire", PDF p. 160 (printed p. 146)
death.note: Timeline Review 2. Genesis gives Abraham 175 years, which would end in 1821 BC. Differs from the ussher death year (1821 BC) by 2 years.

death.citation: Raleigh, The History of the World (1617, EEBO-TCP A10357), Chronological Table, sig. 783a
death.note: Year cell "2865 2183 100". The third printed figure 100 is the column "Promise", not a length. To the Reader (sig. 780b): the Julian Period exceeds the yeere of the World by 682.
